#1034. Man City have a striker who will not be stopped and a defence that cannot be trusted

Manchester City surely cannot win the Champions League with a defence leaking goals and a goalkeeper making errors. But when Erling Haaland is in the team, anything seems possible.

This thrilling victory for City perfectly sums up their season: needless goals conceded, Gianluigi Donnarumma making a mistake, followed by Haaland saving the day with a winning goal.

“How can you stop Haaland?” read the headline in the local Volkszeitung newspaper on the morning of this Champions League clash. The answer is that it has been impossible for RB Leipzig.

Leipzig roll out the Red Bull carpet when they face the Norweigan. He has now scored 13 goals against them in nine matches, the most he has scored against a single team during his career. Enzo Maresca gave him the armband here and his winning goal masked more worries for the City head coach in his back line.

A brilliant Man City move finished off by who else but Erling Haaland 🤖 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/cIpvbgJa2O

“I think we need to step up a bit,” said Haaland afterwards. “When we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third – that’s what we have to do. We have to work on that.

“Keeping the ball, when to keep it, when to go, working together offensively and defensively – you can always be better and there’s always a new chance.”

Haaland had the final say in a match where City were gifted the lead through Castello Lukeba’s own goal, before Donnarumma was exposed at his near post by Ridle Baku’s cheeky finish when the City goalkeeper was positioned for a cross.

A moment to forget for Leipzig's Castello Lukeba as his own goal gives Man City the lead🫣 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/64aPm9E7zV

Maresca was not happy either with Antonio Nusa finding a second equaliser for Leipzig after Enzo Fernández had headed City back in front. Haaland had only three touches of the ball in the first half but slid in for the winner when Elliot Anderson broke forward late on.

Antonio Nusa beats Gianluigi Donnarumma and finds the bottom corner to equalise for Leipzig 🇳🇴 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/vCZ0WtQH1P

“You can look at it that it’s difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it’s only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance – you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option,” Haaland added.

This was a victory to bounce back from losing in the Premier League at the weekend, but the question will be how can City mount a title challenge with such a brittle defence. Champions League winners do not leave themselves open at the back like this, and City have now gone seven games without a clean sheet.

Maresca insisted last week that his starting line-up is Donnarumma plus 10 others, but the reality is that Haaland is the guaranteed name on the team sheet. And his goalkeeper’s errors are becoming a problem.

This one added to the goals against Aston Villa and Paris St-Germain that were also on his watch. He could have claimed the cross that led to Brighton’s winner at the weekend too.

Here he went from hero to villain in the space of a few minutes at the start of the second half. Firstly, from kick-off Christoph Baumgartner got close with his angled drive heading towards the top corner until Donnarumma’s fingertips turned the ball around the post. It was a save that had the Italian celebrating like he had scored a goal.

But he had his head in his hands after Leipzig’s next move. Nico O’Reilly could have done better after losing the ball in midfield, then failing to track the overlapping run from Baku. With Red Bull Arena waiting for a cross, Baku had spotted Donnarumma slightly out of position and beat him at the near post. It was superb improvisation, but without doubt a goalkeeping error.

Gianluigi Donnarumma with a huge mistake as Ridle Baku's near-post effort goes straight in 😬 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/r2K0C5jbqm

“A few minutes before he’s done a save that no keeper in the world makes,” Maresca said. “Gigi knows he was not good with the first goal. He’s going to do better.”

Maresca says that Donnarumma will be in goal at the weekend when City face Nottingham Forest and there is no genuine competition for him. But Maresca will know a stable goalkeeper is needed for a title challenge.

City went 2-1 ahead through Fernández just before the hour mark. Iliman Ndiaye floated a ball into the penalty area and the Argentina midfielder timed his run to head into the bottom corner.

Iliman Ndiaye with a superb cross that finds Enzo Fernandez who heads home superbly 🎯 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/oMBypXk7yP

Was this a sign of City stability in the game? Hardly. Leipzig worked the ball around the penalty box until they found an opening, with Nusa finishing powerfully into the bottom corner.

“Both goals are quite silly goals we can avoid,” added Maresca. “We are creating many chances in each game but we need to avoid silly goals. It’s about working more. Understand and analyse. I’m new here, I need to know the players and they need to know me. We can only improve.

“At some point we had four or five clean sheets before and now we are conceding many goals. Some moments you concede, some moments you don’t. When you give away goals like the first one or the one that we gave away in the last games, that is something that we need to avoid.”

The evening was decided by Haaland, sliding in for a tap-in after Anderson had broken through the Leipzig back line. In the context of the group stages, City are within sight of qualification for the knockout stage, but they next face Napoli before visiting Barcelona in what will be the ultimate test of how much they can improve quickly in defence.

It’s the most I’ve scored against one club [13] but I’ve played so many times against them. Leipzig are a good team. [Anderson] has been amazing, an amazing start to his City career. That’s what you expect to be honest. You have to come straight in and perform, It’s not easy. You need time to adapt, time to get to know your new team-mates and coach, which is not easy even for us, and he’s been very impressive. Respect!

Thirteen touches I had today, you say? It’s not the most but what is important is that I help the team to win and I managed to do that today. So I am super happy.

In the end we need to step up a little bit. When we went 1-0 up we should have pushed for the second more and then hopefully the third. That’s what we have to work at. Keep the ball, when to keep it when to go. Working together both offensively and defensively but that’s the good part there’s always a chance to get better. There’s always a new game and our next chance will be in three days.

You can look at [keeping focused to make the right runs despite the lack of touches] in different ways – either 100 minutes is a long time to stay concentrated or 100 minutes is not that long to stay concentrated. I look at it like the second option.

City win the first header from the Leipzig free-kick and the ref blows his whistle for full time.

Enjoyable game, very even until Nusa went off but City, like Arsenal, can bring on their billionaire bomb squad off the bench to turn the screw. And they did so here. City’s defence and goalkeeper are still major worries.

Cherki wastes an opportunity to pass to an unmarked Haaland in the box by trying and failing to force his shot though Orban’s legs. Khusanov has to make a foul to stop a Leipzig break.

Doku blazes a shot over to end a City break after Donnarumma had caught a cross following the free-kick.

Leipzig have a free-kick on the left after a daft Allan foul on Banzuzi. Three more minutes to come.

Terrific save from Vandevooort low to his left, almost clawing it back from behind him with a Stretch Armstrong left arm after Doku’s cross kicked up and struck Haaland’s leg.

Gruda rolls the ball into an empty net after deceiving Donnarumma but both knew he was a mile offside when Gomis’s pass found him.

Haaland hits the post with a right-foot shot from an offside position after either jumping the gun or, more likely, Cherki delaying the pass too long.

Now Cherki thunders a left-foot shot into the crossbar after a good work from Kovacic.

Donnarumma is evidently suffering a crisis of confidence. After an O’Reilly foul on the right. Raum bends a cross/shot towards the back post. Donnarumma backpedals about as quickly as Peter Shilton used to do, caught in no man’s land, and must be relieved to hear the ball thud into the crossbar.

RB Leipzig 2 Man City 3 (Haaland) Slides in at the back post to turn in Anderson’s superb pass. The England midfielder drove into the box, burning past Raum and Banzuzi. That’s Haaland’s 13th career goal against Leipzig.

City have to go all the way back to Donnarumma after Banzuzi heads Fernández’s inswinging corner back to him.

City corner on the left after O’Reilly’s underlapping run catches Leipzig on the back foot.

Well, that was a lively 10 minutes. Ndiaye has gone to the right and Doku is on the left now. The left winger plays a one-two with Cherki, the No 10 giving the ball back with a backheel, then crosses to the back post. Fernández can only reach it at the apex of his jump with the crown of his head and Ndiaye can’t stop it going out for a goalkick.

Enzo, not for the first time, goes down clutching his face when brushed by an opponent’s hand. The crowd whistles him as he does his dying fly act.

RB Leipzig 2 Man City 2 (Nusa) Nkunku, who had just come on for Baumgartner, has the vision to see Nusa running into the box down the left and picked him out with an unusual pass from the middle of goal when most would have expected him to let Roulo have a shot. Nusa ran on to it and whacked a shot into the bottom right.

Antonio Nusa beats Gianluigi Donnarumma and finds the bottom corner to equalise for Leipzig 🇳🇴 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/vCZ0WtQH1P

RB Leipzig 1 Man City 2 (Enzo) Baku gives Ndiaye too much space down the City left and he cuts back on to his right to bend an inswinger towards the six-yard box. Fernandez peels off Lukeba’s shoulder to bury the header. Great cross, great run, great finish.

Iliman Ndiaye with a superb cross that finds Enzo Fernandez who heads home superbly 🎯 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/oMBypXk7yP

City let Baku pile down the right again and get a shot off from inside the box. Donnarumma stoops to catch it and spills it but manages to dive forward to scoop it away before Romulo could pounce, taking the player as well as the ball. Leipzig want a penalty but the keeper got enough of the ball.

Golden chance for Haaland when Cherki’s pass ricochets off Banzuzi to the centre-forward by the penalty spot. He strikes it first time with his right foot but Vandervoort is equal to it, swooping low to his left to keep it out with a strong left wrist.

RB Leipzig 1 Man City 1 (Baku) Seamus Coleman once scored a goal against Leeds like that. The right-back was sent down the right by Gruda’s cute pass. The keeper, Donnarumma, positioned himself for the cross and left his near post unguarded and Baku threaded it through the yawning gap.

Gianluigi Donnarumma with a huge mistake as Ridle Baku's near-post effort goes straight in 😬 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/r2K0C5jbqm

Haaland’s fourth touch is to head the corner out of the box but Leipzig move it back infield to Baumgartner who leathers a shot from 18 yards that Donnarumma soars to tip round the post.

TNT Sports tells us that Haaland had three touches in the first 45 minutes. Leipzig start at a fair lick by sending Nusa down the left and he cuts in on his right to try to score the kind of goal that used to be a Thierry Henry speciality, bent into the top right. It may have been creeping in but more likely not. Donnarumma claws it round the post for a corner playing the percentages.

Some bright moments for the home side who are overplaying in attack much as Arshavin-era Arsenal used to do. City have looked good on the break but have failed to exploit Haaland’s channel running and ability to ghost away from Orban and Lukeba with the right pass.

Leipzig trying to send a message to the fans with his half-time playlist: I Will Survive and Don’t Stop Believing so far.

Haaland is going to tear a strip off his team-mates at half-time. They keep ignoring his runs. It’s as if they think he’s a decoy.

Haaland’s first notable chance quickly follows the goal, a back-post header from O’Reilly’s left-wing cross but he could not get enough purchase on the ball.

Leipzig 0 Man City 1 (Lukeba og) A long diagonal from Cherki plays O’Reilly in down the left. He picks up his head and crosses low, too far in front of Haaland. Foden traps Banzuzi’s defensive header with his right to shift it on to his left then bends a shot that goes whistling past the left post.

Anderson snaps into the press and opens the door down the right for Ndiaye who can’t get away from Raum.

Baku is booked for scything down O’Reilly who had laid the ball off long before Baku dived in.

Gruda butchers a very good chance on the right of the City box after Fernandez and Cherki are caught upfield and leave Anderson minding the shop all alone. Baku, coming round Gruda, was screaming for the lay-up to shoot but Gruda took it on himself and scuffed it tamely wide.

Anderson is a foul magnet. Opponents keep catching and clipping him.

Baumgartner heeds the crowd’s advice and has a pop from 25 yards with a right-foot curling effort that doesn’t bend back in sufficiently. Donnarumma paid it the compliment of a full-length dive to his left but it was never on target.

Leipzig are guilty of overelaboration in and around the City box. Too many tricks and flicks, not enough shots and crosses. Haaland is giving his team-mates some jip for not reading his runs.

Cherki pings a pass out to Enzo on the right and he slips as he tries to cross, his momentum as he fell forcing the cross deeper than he had planned and it sails beyond a visibly frustrated Haaland who keeps making good runs but has yet to be found.

City are dicing with danger by letting Nusa run at them from positions on both wings and through the middle. They manage to stop him threading ir flicking passes through to Romulo twice in the space of 30 seconds but it would be less stressful to cut it off at source further away from their goal.

City can’t hang on to the ball in high areas, yielding possession too cheaply and Leipzig swarm forward down the right with City scrambling back. When the cut-back is played into the box, it is behind the first wave of Leipzig runners but galloping behind is Raum, the cavalry. He gets there and crashes a shot with his left that is blocked.

A replay of Donnarumma’s ‘save’ show that it was on target and the keeper could easily have squirted it through his hands into the goal. Small wonder he rotated his head as if auditioning for a part in the Exorcist to look back in relief.

Leipzig take the corner short and City push them back and try to start a counter that ends when Baumgartner takes Anderson out with a rash sliding tackle that upends the England midfielder.

Nusa, who has licence to roam, pops up on the right wing and cuts inside past Guéhi, dribbling across the 18-yard line before thumping a rising shot that Donnarumma puts his hands above his hands to catch but doesn’t cling on. He managed to do enough to slap it over the bar, though. I think it was always going to vault the crossbar. Corner for Leipzig.

Haaland, who hasn’t had a kick, closes the keeper Vandevoort down from his blindside and he flaps at his clearance, ballooning it straight tp Foden, 30 yards from goal. Banzuzi makes sure Foden doesn’t make them pay.

Leipzig break at pace with O’Reilly caught upfield, switching it to their left and running 50 yards towards the City box but Nunes makes an impressive recovery run to win the tackle.

Anderson almost picks up out O’Reilly who had made an underlapping run down the left as Ndiaye lured Baku out to the wing. But Orban stops O’Reilly spinning on to the pass.

Ndiaye rides his luck and two tackles before the ball just skips away form him as he was closing towards the 18-yard line but Leipzig botch the clearance and Foden feeds a lovely pass in from the right to Cherki who opens his body and wraps a left-foot shot the wrong side of the left post.

Cherki intercepts a pass meant for Nusa but goes backwards instead of looking for Foden down the right, killing the impetus of an unexpected interception.

Nusa stretches his legs down the left after a clumsy lay-off from Cherki and shifts the ball inside to meet Romulo’s run between Khusanov and Nunes but Nunes sticks with him and forces him deep, so close to the byline in fact that his attempt to square it goes straight to Donnarumma.

Khusanov, under pressure from Romulo, squeezes a pass that deflects off him and goes out for a City throw-in.

After a moment’s silence for Jesús de Miguel who was killed after being injured while playing for Tenerife earlier this week, Manchester City kick off, attacking from left to right. They are in black with yellow trim, the colours of the bee emblem of the city of Manchester. Leipzig are in white with red bits. City move the ball back to Donnarumma who instigates and attack up the left that the home side deals with easily and when they try again Baku heads Nunes’ long ball away.

City only have a small portion of the stadium for travelling support – but the boos for the Champions League anthem is heard loud and clear. There are a few fans dressed up as sheikhs too.

Not freezing here in Leipzig but temperatures are dropping. City are still out there warming up, with Haaland leading the shooting practice. Leipzig have headed inside.

We know each other very well and we’re almost like brothers. I know his philosophy and how he wants to play. Enzo is a winner and he’ll be looking to win trophies with Manchester City.

I had three fantastic years at Manchester City myself, but that was a long time ago,” he said. “Being a coach is a completely different job.

[Here] the players needed time to get to know me, and I needed time to get to know them but we’ve played well in our last three games.

We’ve become more solid and put in an excellent performance both on and off the ball at Schalke.

We’ll try to produce the same kind of display at home against a top-quality side.

Obviously I had the unfortunate red card against Man Utd but I think the break did me good. I came back really fresh and sharp.

I’ve been involved in a lot of goals lately and I’ve been really happy with my own performance.

Hopefully I can get back to that level. I think I’m starting to get back there now. Hopefully I keep growing and getting better.

It is one of those things [being dropped by Thomas Tuchel]. Football is full of ups and downs and it’s one of those things you can’t control.

You just have to keep trying your best on the field and keep putting in performances. Hopefully, one day, the call-up might come back.

Erling Haaland, an ex-Red Bull player after his spell with their Salzburg team, is captain and leads the team out at Red Bull Arena.

Nkunku starts on the bench. Leipzig have been playing 4-5-1 since that 4-1 gubbing at the Bernabéu and it looks like Demichelis has stuck with it for City.

#1033. China's influence in the gaming industry is growing

Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

In a dark underground hideout, dim light spills from a handful of oil lamps. A comrade fiddles with a rifle. A red flag hangs on one of the roughly hewn stone walls, bearing a hammer and sickle on a white star — the symbol of the ChineseWorkers' and Peasants' Red Army. Weapons are scattered on the ground. One is picked up, and soon the action moves into the snowy forest, where gunfire erupts among the trees.

Such a scene could fit in a new installment of "Call of Duty," the popular first-person shooter game that transports players to battlefields past, present, and future. But it is actually from "The Defiant." The game is currently being developed by the Chinese studio Hoothanes Technology in Hangzhou. It tells the story of Chinese forces fending off the Japanese army in the 1930s and 1940s.

Developer Connor Xu tells DW the weapons featured in the game are unique. They were used only in Asia and are therefore unfamiliar to many Western players, he says. The same goes for the story, which Xu says has never before been told in a video game.

"The Defiant" is also designed to appeal to an international audience. In just a few years, China has emerged as a major player in the global gaming industry despite strict regulations, censorship and a former ban on video game consoles.

More than 700 million people in China regularly play video games. According to market research company Newzoo, most consider gaming an important part of their lives. Many use games to stay in touch with friends.

"Games make life more interesting," developer Xu says. "I can try different roles, different stories, different characters, because we only have one life to live, but we can play a role in another story. That's really attractive, I think, to Chinese users."

People in China primarily play games on PCs and smartphones, while consoles are much less common. There are historical reasons for that: While gamers in Europe and North America debated whether PlayStation or Xbox was the better console in the early 2000s, the devices were not officially sold in China between 2000 and 2014. Chinese authorities said the restrictions were intended to protect children and teenagers from becoming addicted to gaming.

Minors in China are currently allowed to play online games for no more than three hours a week. There are no such limits for adults, but gaming is subject to strict controls. Anyone who wants to play must register using their real name and a personal identification number. That effectively allows the state to track who plays what and when, as well as whom they communicate with.

There is also a gray area that the Chinese government appears to tolerate. Some players log in using VPNs, giving them access to games that are not officially available in China. Some younger players use their parents' accounts to get around the limits on gaming time.

Despite its strict controls on underage gamers, China has become increasingly receptive to video games in general, having recognized the industry's enormous economic potential. Early on, games released for Chinese players often appeared to be copies of Western titles. At the same time, Chinese tech companies such as Tencent and NetEase invested in numerous Western gaming companies.

One distinctive feature of the Chinese market is its licensing system. "Unlike a lot of the other big video games markets in the world, China has a tightly regulated and licensed official video games market," George E. Osborn tells DW. The journalist advises NGOs and governments on video games and spoke at the Gamescom congress. In his book "Power Play," he describes how authoritarian states use video games to pursue political objectives.

The rule for all games in China is simple: No license, no sales. "That system essentially forces developers who want to release their video games to go through multiple layers of approval from China's Ministry of Propaganda, Ministry of Culture," Osborn says.

Games are prohibited from containing material that threatens China's unity, sovereignty or territorial integrity, among other restrictions. Pornographic content and gambling are also banned. Games may not incite crimes that threaten national security or spread information authorities believe could disrupt public order.

"The whole point around this criteria is that it's deliberately designed to be pretty vague," Osborn says. Whether a game violates the rules is a matter of interpretation. Sometimes games are altered even after release. In the 2025 action role-playing game "Wuchang: Fallen Feathers," for example, enemies based on famous Chinese figures from the Ming Dynasty suddenly could no longer be killed. Instead, they would collapse from exhaustion.

The Chinese action role-playing game "Black Myth: Wukong" became an unexpected international hit in 2024. By then, it was clear Chinese developers could do more than cater to the domestic market — they could create successful games for a global audience as well. The game was inspired by the 16th-century Chinese literary classic "Journey to the West."

Osborn sees nothing wrong with bringing Chinese culture to audiences around the world. The question, he says, is how much the state actually intervenes in the games themselves. "I think in general, video game players are actually quite deeply skeptical of these kinds of things. They are generally very good at spotting when someone might be selling to them or someone might be propagandizing. And so I think if it's too obvious, it won't work," he says.

Because of the licensing system, Western developers also have to comply with government requirements if they want to sell their games in China. And they do want to, Osborn says, because the market is too big to ignore. "But I think when you start thinking about the potential impact this has on creative standards around the world, I think it's really important that developers ask themselves the question of what will we or won't we compromise on here?"

He fears the real danger lies in self-censorship. That could lead developers, for example, to leave queer characters out of their games. That would represent a major step backward, he says, because games help many people explore their identities.

China is not the only country where games are modified to comply with national regulations. In Germany, for example, symbols that violate the country's constitution, such as the swastika, may not be shown in games unless the game in question explicitly contributes to the country's culture of remembrance. Depictions of extreme violence also have to be removed from German versions.

Glorifying violence is prohibited in China, too, yet Xu's team is still allowed to develop a war game. How does this add up? Xu explains it this way: "I think in this game, the most important thing is not violence. The most important thing is to tell history."

Xu says the team is committed to delivering a historically accurate product. Whether it succeeds will be for historians to judge.

This article was translated from German and edited by Sarah Hucal.

Newcastle United's reliance on the past is costing them dearly in the present after another home defeat

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The cruel irony of Newcastle United’s current predicament is that, for all they are looking to the future, they are too reliant on the past and it is costing them dearly in the present.

As the rain lashed down at St James’ Park on Monday night, it captured the sodden mood on Tyneside as Everton secured a third straight Premier League win on that famous ground courtesy of Thierno Barry’s second half goal.

Newcastle dropped to 13th in the table after a third defeat in four.

A sell out crowd greeted the final whistle with the sort of indignation which could be construed in a tipping point in their tolerance of the current state of affairs, something Matthias Jaissle insisted he understood as pressure on him grows.

"I was aware of the anger,” he told reporters afterwards. “Big frustration, big disappointment because we couldn't transfer what we saw in the week.

"The team was training at a high level, but since the ref started the game, not much was seen. It's difficult to understand. Of course the fans are frustrated, like we are.

"Unfortunately, we couldn't deliver. Actually, over the whole 90 minutes, it was not our game and our style of playing. That is something we are very frustrated and disappointed about. If you cannot deliver when it counts, then you don't deserve to win.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

With every passing game, it becomes clearer that the framing of the summer may have been wrong. Newcastle knew there would be huge transition, with the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali accounted for in advance.

The departures first of manager Eddie Howe and then captain Bruno Guimaraes just weeks out from the start of the Premier League season were not what the club wanted.

Yet, in an interview with TNT Sports before the 2-2 draw with Bournemouth on September 5, sporting director Ross Wilson insisted the summer had gone to plan “almost in its entirety”.

Out with the old and in with the new; a refresh, Newcastle 2.0. That is what the fans were told. After the success of the first five years under the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, which yielded two Champions League campaigns and a trophy, Newcastle had hit their ceiling and it was necessary to take a step back to move forward again in a more sustainable manner.

Wilson spoke of giving youth a chance and taking risks - a fresh identity he hoped would help the club become more competitive in the long run. More than £200m was spent on eight new players, but the problem is Jaissle does not seem to count on a number of them.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m, but the 20-year-old Ivorian has barely featured; the same can be said for £35m midfielder Aladji Bamba.

Following a stellar performance in the victory over Hull City on September 19, it was hoped Dutch teenager Sean Steur would be given more responsibility. His substitute appearance shortly after Barry’s opener was his first league appearance since.

The bold strategy set out has yet to come to fruition. It is hard to blame Jaissle for not having more trust, but the upshot is that Guimaraes’ replacement right now looks to be Joe Willock, a player who, it was almost universally felt for as long as a couple of years, had no future at Newcastle.

Replacing Alexander Isak’s goals, a year after his acrimonious departure for Liverpool, is the responsibility of Will Osula, his former understudy, despite £175m being spent on strikers since 2025.

Harvey Barnes, consistently used as a bit-part player while Gordon shone on the left, has been given his opportunity. At present, he simply isn’t taking it.

There are so many others, too. Jaissle brought Fabian Schar and Dan Burn back into the fold ahead of the victory over Crystal Palace last Sunday and it worked perfectly. Since returning from injury, too, Joelinton has been a regular in an unfamiliar deep midfield role, but his physicality and leadership are seen as too important to go without.

Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest for Jacob Murphy on transfer deadline day and he too has featured regularly this season.

All of these players were crucial in Newcastle’s recent success, but by complimenting the best players in the team. Now Isak, Guimaraes, Tonali and Gordon have left, making them more prominent naturally reduces the overall quality, and it is not hard to understand the sort of impact that has on progress.

Long-term, the hope is that Steur, Bamba and Toure will develop into players capable of filling the boots of the players who have gone. They certainly have the profile and potential to do so. But right now, there is a void in Newcastle's squad, an imbalance between its character and quality. Left unchecked, the consequences could be dire.

The iconic former Reds forward and manager had a strange day out at Anfield back in 1995 with his Blackburn side going for the title

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

You couldn't have written it. On the final day of the 1994/95 Premier League season, Kenny Dalglish returned in front of the Anfield crowd that adored him and were cheering him on - but as manager of their opposition, Blackburn Rovers, who needed results to go their way to win the league.

The situation was this: if Blackburn lost, and Manchester United won away to West Ham, then Alex Ferguson's side would win the title at Rovers' expense. Indeed, Ferguson openly suggested that Liverpool may be less than up for the occasion.

But the now-Sir Kenny believes the now-Sir Alex was absolutely entitled to push that agenda - and that, in fact, he wouldn't have been doing his job properly if he hadn't.

As it happened, Blackburn did lose... but Man United could only draw at West Ham, thus handing the title to Blackburn. Sir Kenny recently told FourFourTwo: “In 1994-95, we were competing against Manchester United for the title, but there was no animosity between me and Alex Ferguson.

"As managers, you were in competition with everybody; what's wrong with that? He was going to speak up for his club, to put ideas into people's minds or dismiss other people's ideas, and I was the same.

"If you weren't supporting your club, the punters were going to be unhappy, so he had every right to do it. He was as good as gold.

"The last game of the season was at Anfield – it was always amazing to go back to Anfield, and the Liverpool punters wanted us to win that day.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"It's not often that they go to Anfield and want the opposition to win, is it?

"If you're not going to win the league at home, then for me, that was a fairy tale to win it at Anfield.

"The TV people wouldn't tell us what the score was from Manchester United's game at West Ham, but people were cheering when their game finished, and it came to pass that we were champions.

"You think about where a lot of those boys were before, and we didn't have a great deal of experience of players winning trophies for previous teams.

"But it was just, ‘Get on with it, you are where you are because you deserve to be there, so just do your best.'

"When I saw Jack Walker after the game, he couldn't speak.

"He'd played a huge, huge part in the financial support, and he never, ever interfered.

"To see somebody of his business strength in tears, you'd think he'd done something wrong - but they were tears of joy

#1030. Chipotle shares rise 7% after CEO says same-store sales growth will continue

Chipotle Mexican Grill on Wednesday reported mixed quarterly results and said its restaurant-level operating margin shrank.

But the burrito chain saw traffic and same-store sales grow during the quarter as low-income consumers spent more, bucking industry trends, and CEO Scott Boatwright projected a strong finish to the year.

Shares of the company rose 7% in extended trading.

"Broader consumer and industry headwinds may continue, but initiatives across our recipe for growth strategy are building and giving us more tools to win in any environment," Boatwright said on the company's earnings conference call. "We are still in the early stages of this work, and it's gaining traction."

Like the broader restaurant industry, Chipotle saw trends soften in early October, although executives said its traffic has returned to growth since then. Boatwright said the company has "high confidence" in its performance for the rest of the fourth quarter.

"We feel very confident that November and December set up very well for us," Boatwright said.

Chief Financial Officer Adam Rymer said the company expects fourth-quarter same-store sales growth of about 2%.

Here's what the company reported for the period ended Sept. 30 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

Chipotle reported fiscal third-quarter net income of $339.9 million, or 27 cents per share, down from $382.1 million, or 29 cents per share, a year earlier. The company's restaurant-level operating margin fell from 24.5% to 23.3%.

Excluding restaurant asset impairment charges and stock-based compensation, the company earned 27 cents per share.

Net sales rose 9.6% to $3.29 billion, fueled by the chain's new restaurants. During the quarter, Chipotle opened 84 company-owned restaurants and five international locations run by licensees.

In the second half of July, Chipotle said it started to see sales pull back as diners grew concerned about consuming raw lettuce due to cyclospora, although its own supply was never tied to an outbreak. Then in August, the chain disclosed that it had temporarily pulled jalapenos from Minnesota restaurants after learning its supply was potentially linked to a salmonella outbreak.

Still, the chain was able to report same-store sales growth for its third straight quarter, shaking off last year's traffic woes.

Sales at stores open at least 13 months increased 2.1%, lifted by a 1.3% bump in average check.

For the first time this year, low-income consumers during the quarter outperformed the high-income cohort at its restaurants, Boatwright said. And discounts aren't the reason — low-income consumers spent the most in September, when promotions were at their low point during the quarter, he told analysts.

For the full year, Chipotle reiterated its previous forecast that its same-store sales will increase by a low-single-digit percentage.

Looking ahead to 2027, the company is projecting that it will open between 340 and 360 new company-owned locations in the U.S. and Canada and around 15 to 25 international restaurants.

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has agreed his next transfer.

The Argentine centre-back was sent off at the weekend for Man United against Chelsea in manager Michael Carrick's third successive defeat, in what is fast becoming a nightmare campaign at the club.

It follows comments that Martinez made criticising the Red Devils' hierarchy, as things begin to unravel at Old Trafford.

Martinez joined Manchester United from Ajax in 2022 in a move worth £57 million, as reported by the BBC, with the Red Devils beating Arsenal to the signing of the defender and then-manager Erik ten Hag reuniting with one of his generals from the Johan Cruyff Arena.

#1028. FedEx beats expectations, raises outlook in first report since calendar adjustment

FedEx on Wednesday reported quarterly earnings that beat Wall Street expectations on the top and bottom lines and raised its full-year outlook for its newly realigned fiscal year.

Shares of the company fell slightly in extended trading.

Here's how the company performed for the period ended Sept. 30 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

The company reported net income for the quarter of $290 million, or $1.21 per share, compared with $650 million, or $2.73 per share, during the comparable period a year prior. Adjusting for one-time items — including losses related to short-term investments, gains on the extinguishment of debt and certain restructuring costs — FedEx reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.74.

It marks the first report of FedEx's realigned fiscal year, moving the end of its calendar from May 31 to Dec. 31. The report also comes after the company successfully spun out FedEx Freight into a separate publicly traded company.

FedEx said its express U.S. segment operating income increased in the quarter, primarily driven by higher package yields and volume.

"As our strong operating results and adjusted free cash flow demonstrate, FedEx is winning across high-value market segments while we optimize our network, driving an increase to our full-year outlook," CEO Raj Subramaniam said in a statement.

For the full year, the company is now expecting adjusted earnings per share of between $18 and $18.60, compared with a prior range of $16.90 to $18.10. FedEx also said it's revising its 2026 revenue growth expectation to a roughly 12% year-over-year increase, up from previous guidance of an 11% increase.

Earlier this week, FedEx named former AutoZone executive Jamere Jackson as the company's new chief financial officer, effective Nov. 30. He replaces Claude Russ, who served as the interim CFO since June 1. John Dietrich was announced as stepping down from that role in April.

#1025. Liverpool’s horror night underlines Andoni Iraola’s Champions League gamble

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool: Iraola defended making changes to his team but a late collapse in Istanbul highlighted the challenge of leading such a lopsided squad across multiple fronts

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

As Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo stood on the touchline in Istanbul, it was clear to see that Andoni Iraola needed some impact. Within minutes, he got it, as Isak headed in Gakpo’s cross to restore Liverpool’s lead at Fenerbahce. But Iraola’s triple-change did not resolve Liverpool’s biggest issue as they dropped points in the Champions League for the first time this season and slipped to consecutive defeats in all competitions: that his team were disorganised and lacked cohesion. As the visitors twice conceded late on to give up their lead for the second time, a 3-2 defeat to Dirk Kuyt’s side was Liverpool’s worst night since Iraola took charge.

It can put be down as a blip, particularly as the nature of the Champions League league phase – and Liverpool starting their campaign with three wins from three – meant they faced a hostile crowd and intimidating atmosphere in Istanbul but very little actual jeopardy. That was reflected in Iraola’s line-up as he tried out a strikerless attack that featured Bradley Barcola, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with Isak and Gakpo kept in reserve. The move backfired. Barcola, so promising attacking from the left against Arsenal on Sunday, carried little threat as he played in the unfamiliar central role. Liverpool missed a presence up front, but it was also their lapses in defence that cost them.

“Cheap goals. Messy goals,” Iraola said. Liverpool conceded three times from set-pieces but if Mason Greenwood’s deflected free-kick was unlucky then losing Archie Brown at the back post from a corner was sloppy and Vedat Muriqi rising in the box following a long throw, surrounded by red shirts but otherwise unopposed, was just not good enough. It was also the third time in as many games in the Champions League that Liverpool had shipped three. They switched off late on while leading Lask in Austria before a dismal start against Villarreal at Anfield. At Fenerbahce, it felt as if there was an element of chaos throughout.

Afterwards, Iraola defended making five changes from Sunday’s 1-0 defeat to Arsenal. The nature of Liverpool’s lopsided squad has meant that Iraola has had to trust his options throughout a demanding period of six games in 18 days. At Fenerbahce, Iraola largely replicated the approach of Liverpool’s Carabao Cup win against Chelsea last week, keeping his first-choice attacking options back before gradually adding strength later on. But also making changes in defence – with Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas withdrawn late on – was a gamble and did not help Liverpool’s security, instead adding to their instability.

“We have done this not just today, we have done it all season,” Iraola said in his defence. “All the games midweek we have been changing four or five as it’s impossible to retain the starting XI. I trust the squad to sustain the level and I don’t think it is the main reason why we lost. We have to look more at how we conceded the goals as the reason we didn’t win.”

Fenerbahce had lost 6-0 to Aston Villa just last month and were in a sorry state following the resignation of Ismail Kartal last week. No wonder interim boss Kuyt hailed victory over his former team as a “miracle”. But it was a wake-up call for Liverpool in the Champions League, too, while underlining the task Iraola faces to guide this curiously assembled squad on multiple fronts.

An individual indirectly criticised by Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez is set to leave the club, according to reports

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Manchester United’s current predicament could get worse before it gets better, with reports in Germany suggesting that director of recruitment Christopher Vivell is on the verge of joining Bayern Munich.

As the Old Trafford hierarchy wrestles with growing scrutiny, accusations of a lack of leadership and a fractured dressing room, the loss of one of their footballing strategy leads threatens to cause further operational problems.

According to a report from Sport Witness, Vivell is being lined up by Bayern Munich.

The German executive’s potential exit comes at an inopportune time for the Red Devils, who are currently navigating issues on and off the pitch.

Vivell’s tenure in Manchester has been relatively brief but significant. Initially brought in ahead of the 2024/25 season on a short-term, interim basis, his influence within the new INEOS-led regime quickly grew.

By February 2025, Man United had seen enough to appoint him as their full-time director of recruitment, giving him responsibility to oversee the club’s global talent identification and squad-building.

However, Vivell's long-term vision now appears to have been compromised by the current chaos and lack of results at Old Trafford.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Man United are enduring a disastrous spell at present with one win from their opening nine Premier League games this season, leaving them languishing at the wrong end of the table.

Their cup exploits have offered little relief, after they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton and Hove Albion, and most recently suffered a damaging Champions League defeat away to Atletico Madrid.

At the centre of it all is first-team boss Michael Carrick, whose own future hangs in the balance. The manager is essentially operating under a stay of execution with many expecting the axe to swing before long.

It is the belief of some Man United outsiders that a lack of unified leadership in key positions has negatively impacted the club's decision-making processes.

Reports indicate that Vivell and director of football Jason Wilcox do not see eye-to-eye over the succession plan should Carrick be formally dismissed. While the club has reportedly shortlisted high-profile candidates, including Julian Nagelsmann, Fabian Hurzeler, and Antonio Conte, the inability of the football leadership team to align on a common direction has only exacerbated the crisis.

If Vivell were to accept Bayern Munich’s overtures, it would leave a void in Man United's recruitment department just as the club faces the prospect of yet another mid-season managerial change. Having an established working relationship with Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund, Vivell is, on paper at least, a natural fit for the German giants.

With the January transfer window fast approaching and Carrick’s future unclear, Manchester United can ill afford to lose their recruitment chief.

#1023. Champions League power rankings: PSG remain a joke – but who is catching them?

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are the only teams to still have 100 per cent records after Liverpool’s defeat at Fenerbahce

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

It was largely business as usual in matchweek four of the Champions League as Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona kept on scoring and Arsenal and Bayern Munich returned to winning ways while remaining unbeaten.

But the story of the round belonged to Como, who made history by beating Lens 9-1 away from home and equalling the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League game. Cesc Fabregas’s impressive side now sit fourth in the league phase standings, behind PSG, Real Madrid and Arsenal.

Meanwhile, there was a frustrating defeat for Liverpool at Fenerbahce, but Manchester United produced a stunning comeback to beat Roma and potentially save Michael Carrick’s job, with Matheus Cunha scoring twice on a remarkable night at Old Trafford.

We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season.

Agree or disagree with our standings? Let us know and have your say in the comments below.

The reigning champions are making a mockery of suggestions that they are slow starters in the Champions League. Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions finished outside the top eight in both of their previous successes but have started this campaign on fire in Europe. PSG were 4-0 up after just 17 minutes at Villarreal, and that was without Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. The French champions will be without the brilliant Georgian for the rest of the season after he suffered a ruptured ACL but they remain the team to beat.

Defeats to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in LaLiga ended their winning start under Hansi Flick and perhaps raised the same concerns over whether their defence holds up come the knockout stages. But Lamine Yamal is arguably the world’s best player on current form and Raphinha isn’t too bad, either. The Brazilian made it an astonishing 19 goals and three assists in just 13 matches across LaLiga and the Champions League with his double in the 3-0 win over Aston Villa at Camp Nou.

Mikel Arteta’s got the result they needed in Prague, even if a difficult second-half performance made it a bit of a struggle. An entertaining draw last time out at Bayern Munich, who have such a strong home record, gave a good account of whether the Premier League champions can take the next step against a heavyweight side in the business end of the Champions League.

Bayern returned to winning ways with a professional win against Atletico Madrid – and the big surprise was that Harry Kane was not on the scoresheet. The Ballon d’Or holder’s 10-match scoring run in the Champions League came to an end at the Metropolitano, missing the chance to equal Cristiano Ronaldo’s record. But Bayern rolled on.

Perhaps chaos is the new normal under Jose Mourinho. Real Madrid trailed late on in Athens but Kylian Mbappe equalised before Fede Valverde scored a stunning winner in stoppage time. Jude Bellingham also scored an outrageous flick. Somehow with maximum points, despite trailing Roma 3-1 at the Stadio Olimpico, and Inter and RB Leipzig spurning chances to take the lead at the Bernabeu, the 15-time Champions League winners continue to find a way.

Back-to-back defeats in the Premier League have the shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well. But a battling win at RB Leipzig, with a customary Erling Haaland goal, was a good response, even if City have now gone seven games without a clean sheet. Next up: the return of Kevin De Bruyne with Napoli, followed by a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona.

Liverpool have conceded three goals in three consecutive games in the Champions League or European Cup for the first time and the manner of their “messy” collapse against Fenerbahce was a concern. The nature of Liverpool’s squad means Andoni Iraola has needed to rotate in Champions League but Liverpool’s performance in Istanbul underlined the task he faces. In-form Club Brugge can’t be taken lightly after the international break.

Despite defeat in the Camp Nou, you get the feeling that Unai Emery’s new-look Aston Villa will have learned a lot from their meeting with Barcelona. They had moments of threat, too. Bright showings from the refreshed attacking line-up of Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi, Ibrahim Mbaye and Alysson have helped the Europa League winners retaining their identity under Emery despite the huge squad turnover in the summer.

After starting with back-to-back defeats, how badly Inter needed to respond with back-to-back wins. A comfortable win at Feyenoord also came after Saturday’s Milan derby defeat, with Pio Esposito stepping up amid Lautaro Martinez’s continued absence.

WOW. If Como announced themselves by thrashing Manchester United, the Champions League debutants stole the show this week with a NINE-goal dismantling of poor Lens. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side became the first team to score nine goals away from home in the Champions League or European Cup since 1971. The Italian side are certainly making a name for themselves. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase are going to be fascinating.

Liverpool haven't attacked with much gusto in recent weeks - and might lose one of their forwards this winter

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Liverpool look likely to sell one of their forwards this summer.

The Reds invested heavily in attack over the summer, bringing in Bradley Barcola for over £100 million and adding Victor Munoz to their ranks, too, as the club waved goodbye to Mohamed Salah after nine years of service.

With new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola having plenty of options to choose from in his frontline, however, there has been a slight imbalance, which may be fixed in the winter winter.

Despite the wealth of riches that Liverpool have in attack, it's safe to say that Iraola is still working out his best XI, with the frontline stuttering in recent weeks, and the Basque's side failing to register a shot on target against Arsenal at the weekend.

While Alexander Isak has been in form and Cody Gakpo has looked reborn under the new manager, there are still questions to be answered about where Barcola fits into the picture, how to get the best out of Florian Wirtz, whether Munoz or Rio Ngumoha play on the right flank, and where to play Hugo Ekitike when he returns from injury.

One star who has struggled for game time this season, however, is Federico Chiesa, who TEAMtalk now report is close to leaving the club.

Describing the Italian as “suffering”, Chiesa moved to Anfield in 2024, but made just 14 appearances in all competitions in his first season, as he became just the second Italian player ever to win the Premier League.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Injuries have heavily impacted the 29-year-old's time in England, and now, it's being claimed that he could well return to his homeland, having played just once all season under Iraola.

Chiesa has been consistently linked with Serie A sides during his two years on Merseyside, having failed to hold down a first-team spot – which now seems increasingly unlikely given the options that Liverpool now have.

FourFourTwo understands that the Merseysiders even came close over the summer to signing Yankuba Minteh to strengthen at right-wing, only for the Gambian's move to be called off due to his injury.

Liverpool are still in transition, with the futures of several stars such as Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister still unclear.

Chiesa is worth €10 million, according to Transfermarkt. Liverpool travel to Fenerbahce this week as Champions League action continues this week.
